personal.bio: I'm a first-year Master's student in Electrical and Computer Engineering at UC San Diego, specializing in Machine Learning and Data Science. I'm deeply curious about how intelligent systems reason, collaborate, and evolve—especially when grounded in strong data foundations and thoughtful system design. My interests lie in Agentic AI, multi-agent collaboration, and the full lifecycle of large language models—from fine-tuning and post-training to alignment, safety, and inference optimization. I enjoy exploring how LLMs can be orchestrated as reliable, goal-driven agents, how they communicate with each other, and how we can design guardrails that make these systems both powerful and trustworthy. I consider myself a robust learner—someone who learns by building, questioning assumptions, and continuously experimenting. I'm always curious about new ideas, emerging research, and practical techniques that push AI systems closer to real-world usefulness. I'm particularly drawn to problems at the intersection of modeling, systems, and product thinking, where insights translate into decisions and behavior. I'm open to collaboration, research discussions, and building things with people who enjoy thinking deeply about AI, data, and impact.
